messages:
Maria Chen: FYI hitting a nasty typing leak when using the JS SDK in an Edge worker built as ESM. It shows up as generics resolving to `any` after bundling.
Kevin Ortiz: ugh, repro steps?
Maria Chen: Small sample repo. TS 5.2, esbuild bundle target=es2020, tsconfig `module: "esnext"`, `declaration: true`. In Node the types are fine, but after bundling for edge overloads collapse and `unknown` becomes `any` in inference.
Sasha Ilyin: Do you mean runtime or just what consumers see in their editors?
Maria Chen: Types only — consumers get degraded typings when they `npm install` our package built that way. Example snippet: 

```
export function callApi<T>(input: T): Promise<T>
export function callApi(input: unknown) { /* impl */ }
```

When emitted the d.ts sometimes ends up as `callApi(input: any): Promise<any>` for the bundled build.

Samir Patel: Sounds like a declaration emit + overload + downleveling issue. Which bundler/config is used in the published build?
Maria Chen: esbuild with `bundle: true` for the edge artifact. Also repro'd with Vite dev build (esbuild under the hood).
Kevin Ortiz: Any quick workaround?
Maria Chen: Workaround for now: set `declaration: false` for the bundle and produce `.d.ts` with a separate `tsc --emitDeclarationOnly` step. That preserves overloads in the generated d.ts consumers see. Also toggling `esModuleInterop` changed consumer experience.
Sasha Ilyin: We should add a small matrix to the sample repo showing: `bundle-only`, `tsc:dts`, and consumer install checks. Also document `exports`/`types` fields for dual ESM/CJS packages.
Samir Patel: Also verify `package.json` `types` points to the right file. If bundler emits `dist/index.mjs` and `dist/index.mjs.d.ts` but `types` points to `dist/index.d.ts`, consumers will pick the wrong declarations.
Maria Chen: That was exactly it in the repro — `types` was stale and pointed at the wrong path.
Kevin Ortiz: Action items?
Sasha Ilyin: 1) Add `examples/edge-typing-repro` with minimal build and consumer check (Maria). 2) CI job that installs the built package and runs `tsc --noEmit` in a consumer project to catch regressions (Samir). 3) Docs PR with guidance for SDK authors on ESM/CJS + edge + overload caveats (Kevin).
Maria Chen: I'll open the repro PR and include a short README with suggested tsconfig flags: prefer `emitDeclarationOnly` via `tsc` for dts, keep `module: "esnext"` for runtime bundle, and call out `skipLibCheck: true` only as last resort. Also recommend using explicit generics instead of relying on inference around `unknown`.
Samir Patel: Consider adding `typesVersions` in package.json so TS can resolve different d.ts per module type if we need to.
Maria Chen: Good idea, I'll sketch that in the PR. Tagging @dev-bot to track.
dev-bot: Created issue #3124: "edge-sdk: typing leak for overloads + bundlers" assigned to @Maria Chen :spiral_calendar:
Kevin Ortiz: Thanks — please link the example from the SDK onboarding docs once PR lands.
Maria Chen: Will do :thumbsup:
